step_by_step_reasoning:
1. Identified user client actor (UserConsumerWebMobile) connecting via Route 53 for DNS resolution.
2. Route 53 routes request paths to CloudFront for static content/caching to reduce latency and to ELB for dynamic application requests.
3. ELB routes application traffic into an EKS cluster executing microservices.
4. Microservices query ElastiCache first for fast access/caching, falling back to RDS databases for evaluation/transactional data.
5. AWS Glue extracts data from RDS, writes it into an S3 data lake, and then loads structured/unstructured datasets into Amazon Redshift for data warehousing, analytics, and AI algorithms.

graph.name: Anima Educação Cloud Migration Architecture
graph.notes: Anima Educação migrated from an on-premises monolith to AWS using EKS microservices, RDS, ElastiCache, and a data lake pipeline featuring Glue, S3, and Redshift.

edges.notes: Student request hits Route 53 for DNS resolution.
Route 53 directs request to CloudFront for cached content.
Route 53 directs request to ELB for dynamic backend processing.
ELB forwards traffic into EKS cluster microservices.
Microservice attempts to load data from ElastiCache.
Microservice connects to RDS if cache miss occurs.
Glue extracts transactional data from RDS databases.
Glue loads extracted data into Amazon S3 data lake.
Data is loaded from S3 into Redshift for analytics and AI processing.
